landmarks.name: Lady Bird Lake
landmarks.fact: Named after First Lady Lady Bird Johnson, this reservoir on the Colorado River is a central recreation hub in Austin.

landmarks.name: Boardwalk at Lady Bird Lake
landmarks.fact: This boardwalk section of the Ann and Roy Butler Trail stretches over water, connecting gaps along the lake's southern shore.

landmarks.name: Ann W. Richards Congress Avenue Bridge
landmarks.fact: Famous for housing the world's largest urban bat colony, millions of Mexican free-tailed bats emerge from beneath it at sunset.

landmarks.name: Auditorium Shores at Town Lake Metropolitan Park
landmarks.fact: Auditorium Shores is an iconic urban park along Lady Bird Lake that hosts outdoor concerts, festivals, and community gatherings.

landmarks.name: The Independent
landmarks.fact: Nicknamed the 'Jenga Tower' due to its offset architecture, this 58-story skyscraper is a distinct feature of Austin's skyline.

landmarks.name: James D. Pfluger Pedestrian Bridge
landmarks.fact: A dedicated pedestrian and bicycle bridge crossing Lady Bird Lake, offering panoramic views of downtown Austin.

landmarks.name: Mexic-Arte Museum
landmarks.fact: Located on Congress Avenue, this museum celebrates Mexican, Latino, and Latin American art and culture through exhibitions and educational programs.
